web_evidence.title: Exploring Jim Kay's illustrations of Diagon Alley
web_evidence.note: Bloomsbury's authorized interior extract from the same work under its UK title sustains external narration of Hagrid and Harry and reports Harry's perceptions and wishes in third person.

web_evidence.title: Bringing Harry Potter to Sweden: The Harry Potter Septology Illuminated by Its Swedish Translation
web_evidence.note: A Stockholm University literary thesis identifies the novels' principal mode as third-person limited through Harry and specifically explains that Stone's opening shifts to an all-knowing authority rather than to a participating first-person narrator.

web_evidence.title: DSC-3 English: Elements of the Novel
web_evidence.note: University instructional analysis explicitly states that Sorcerer's Stone has a third-person narrator who is not part of the story, usually follows Harry's perspective, and sometimes becomes omniscient.

web_evidence.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone: Key Facts
web_evidence.note: The book-specific guide explicitly describes a detached third-person observer uninvolved in the action, mostly close to Harry while shifting focalization to Mr. Dursley in the opening.

person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages q00391 and q00400 expose a nonparticipating narrator describing Harry externally and reporting knowledge or thoughts in third person. The remaining sample is overwhelmingly dialogue, aphorism, song, or inscription and therefore does not compete with the base voice. Bloomsbury's authorized interior extract independently shows the same third-person mode, while two academic sources and a book-specific reference describe the whole-book structure as third person, primarily focalized through Harry with an opening focalization shift. Those shifts are variations within third-person narration, not person alternation. The main limitation is the dialogue-heavy quote sample, but the combined quote, authorized-excerpt, and structural evidence leaves no credible conflict.
